Red Bull: Dominant modern era constructor, rebuilding under new leadership after the seismic 2026 regulation reset.
Ferrari F1: The most storied name in F1, chasing a first constructors' title since 2008 with Hamilton and Leclerc.
McLaren: Reigning constructors' champions and most successful British team in F1 history.
Mercedes: Eight-time consecutive constructors' champions, resurgent in 2026 with the strongest power unit on the grid.
Aston Martin: British outfit transformed by Newey's arrival, hampered by significant Honda power unit challenges in 2026.
Alpine: France's works entry representing Renault's motorsport heritage, a surprise 2026 package with Mercedes power.
Racing Bulls: Red Bull's junior constructor, a proven talent pipeline running Ford-powered machinery from Milton Keynes.
Audi: German giant making its F1 debut in 2026, building toward championship contention with long-term factory ambition.
Haas F1: America's only F1 team, punching above its weight through smart resource management and Ferrari partnership.
Williams Racing: Seven-time constructors' champions rebuilding under fresh investment with Sainz leading the charge.
Cadillac: General Motors' return to F1 as an independent constructor, bringing American ambition back to the grid.
Porsche: Volkswagen Group's iconic sports car brand, bringing decades of motorsport heritage and cutting-edge hybrid expertise to Formula 1.
Toyota: Japanese manufacturing giant returning to F1, backed by Toyota Gazoo Racing's WEC dominance and world-class technical facilities in Cologne.
BYD: Chinese EV pioneer exploring Formula 1 as the sport's electrification aligns with their core technology. The largest EV manufacturer in the world.
BMW: German performance brand with a storied F1 history, having powered Brabham to a championship. A potential return would bring serious intent and budget.
Brabham: One of Formula 1's most legendary constructor names, revived with ambitions to recapture the glory of Jack Brabham's championship-winning era.
Lotus: The most iconic name in Formula 1 history, associated with seven constructors' championships and revolutionary car designs under Colin Chapman.
Jaguar Racing: British manufacturer with an F1 heritage through the early 2000s, returning with renewed ambition and the backing of a storied automotive brand.
